newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australis says no comment on Foxtel talk.
newsitem.headline: Australis says no comment on Foxtel talk.

text.p: Pay television operator Australis Media Ltd said on Monday that it had no comment on a newspaper report that its merger with much larger rival Foxtel would be announced sometime this week.

The Australian Financial Review newspaper said the key shareholders in each company had agreed in principle to merge, with Australis to remain listed and provide a backdoor listing for Foxtel which is owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd and the Australian government's Telstra Corp.
One industry source told Reuters that merger talks had been held and a statement was likely to be issued this week.

A Foxtel spokesman was not available to comment on the newspaper report, which also said any merger would require the approval of the anti-monopolies body -- the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).

The report said News Corp and Telstra would sell their joint venture holding in Foxtel in return for a majority stake in Australis, which has suffered nearly A$500 million of losses in the last two years.

It also said Kerry Packer's listed magazine and investment group Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, which owned 14.4 percent of Australis and was a key financial backer, would remain a major shareholder in the company after the merger.
Australia has three key pay television operators, with Foxtel and Optus Vision having about 200,000 subscribers and Australis struggling to hold 120,000.

Foxtel and Packer's PBL said on June 20 that they had agreed to a rationalisation of the pay-tv industry which analysts said at the time inferred that Foxtel and Australis would eventually merge to attempt the demise of Optus Vision.
Australis shares topped the turnover list on Monday with 3.2 million shares traded. The stock was 1.5 cents higher at 15.5 cents at 11.20 a.m. (0120 GMT).
